headlines: Shared Umbrella Leads to a Longer Walk
Rain Gives Two Strangers a Reason to Talk
One Umbrella Makes Room for Two
bodies: {A} offered {B} shelter beneath an umbrella during a downpour on {street}. They walked past both of their turns before agreeing to meet again.
A rainstorm introduced {A} and {B} under one umbrella. By the time the sky cleared, the two had arranged another walk in better weather.
{A} and {B} began a walk as strangers sharing cover from the rain. They ended it with an invitation to spend a dry afternoon together.

headlines: Umbrella Invitation Ends in a Public Snub
A Dry Shoulder Comes at Someone Else's Expense
Shared Shelter Proves an Uneven Arrangement
bodies: {A} invited {B} beneath an umbrella on {street}, then kept pulling it away to stay dry. {B} abandoned the arrangement after a sharp exchange within earshot of passersby.
An offer of shelter from {A} left {B} standing in the rain anyway. A public argument over the umbrella ended their brief acquaintance.
{B} accepted an invitation to share an umbrella with {A}. The offer lost its charm when {A} refused to share the dry space, and witnesses heard an indignant farewell.

items.era_notes: Use an ordinary umbrella in every decade. Neither outcome establishes marriage or a lasting romantic relationship.

headlines: Clock Face Unearthed with Numbers Facing Down
Garden Dig Reveals an Unusual Timepiece
bodies: {A} uncovered a clock face beneath a garden path, its numbers pressed into the earth. No hands, workings, or maker's mark were found, leaving its purpose unsettled.
A garden repair by {A} revealed an unmarked clock dial buried face down. The finder preserved it for examination, and the Gazette invites information about its origin.
{A} brought an unusual find to public attention: a bare clock face beneath old paving stones. Without hands or a mechanism, it has supplied more questions than answers.

headlines: Buried 'Clock' Proves to Be a Painted Plate
Garden Mystery Ends at the Crockery Shelf
Excavation Finds More Expense Than History
bodies: {A} paid to lift paving stones around what appeared to be a buried clock. Cleaning revealed a cracked plate painted with numbers, and the cost of restoring the path exceeded the find's value.
A supposed clock unearthed by {A} proved to be a numbered plate after cleaning. Public speculation gave way to gentle teasing and a repair bill for the disturbed path.
{A} invited attention to a possible antique clock beneath a garden path. The object was a painted plate, leaving the finder with an ordinary piece of crockery and an unwelcome paving expense.

items.era_notes: Describe a printed Gazette notice in earlier decades and a Gazette request for information in later ones; do not assert supernatural causation.
items.sequel: A later story may resolve buried_clock_face by identifying the dial's origin; require the thread to exist before resolving it.

items.text: They say {A} has been answering letters addressed to {B} without asking permission.
variants: I hope {A} meant to help with the letters for {B}, but permission matters even in a family.
Who has been getting replies from {A} while thinking they were hearing from {B}?

items.text: I hear {A} gave {B} the lead in a backyard play and kept the job of making thunder with a pan.
variants: They say {A} let {B} have the big part; making the thunder sounds like plenty of fun anyway.
{B} supposedly gets the lead, and {A} bangs the thunder pan.
Did {A} give {B} the lead out of kindness, or just discover that thunder gets the loudest applause?

items.text: Word is {A} volunteered {B} to wash every dish after the church supper without mentioning it first.
variants: I hope {A} and {B} sort out that dishwashing promise; a favor is nicer when someone agrees to it.
They say {A} signed {B} up for all the dishes without asking.
Was {A} planning to tell {B} about the washing before supper, or wait until everyone had used two plates?

items.text: People say {A} buys the unclaimed winter coats at rummage sales and leaves them beside the church door.
variants: I hear {A} gets those leftover coats to people who need them; there are worse uses for spare money.
Supposedly {A} buys the leftover coats and leaves them at the church.
If {A} is behind the coats at the church, who keeps cutting the price tags off so carefully?

items.text: They say {A} insists the echo under the bridge has started using a younger voice.
variants: I hear {A} thinks the bridge echo sounds younger; perhaps the river has changed how it carries a voice.
{A} supposedly says the bridge echo has changed its voice.
If {A} hears a younger voice under the bridge, whose voice do people think it is becoming?

warm: Thank you. I had help, and I ought to say so.
That is kind of you to notice.
You have made the work feel a little lighter.
I will remember you said that when the next attempt goes crooked.
I did my best. It is good to hear that it showed.
Well, that is something pleasant to carry home.
curt: I appreciate that. Let us leave it there.
That is decent of you to say.
Thank you. No need to make a gathering of it.
